key_insight: TRACE assigns dense turn-level credit in long-horizon agent RL by converting frozen reference-model gold-answer log-probabilities into state values and using TD differences as per-action rewards.
engineering_relevance: It improves tool-using agents without process labels, a critic, or supervised cold-start fine-tuning, making training more practical for complex search and multi-step automation.
method: Model each tool-call boundary as a state transition
Use a frozen reference model to compute gold-answer log-probabilities and transform them into log-ratio state values
Derive turn-level rewards from one-step temporal-difference changes, which telescope across redundant calls
evidence_signal: On BrowseComp-Plus, TRACE boosted Qwen3-4B from 7.2 to 35.6 and Qwen3-30B-A3B from 8.4 to 42.6, with earlier improvement and faster RL convergence.
watch_item: Because TRACE depends on a frozen reference model’s gold-answer probabilities, its quality may be sensitive to reference-model calibration and to tasks where answer likelihood is noisy or weakly correlated with useful intermediate actions.
paper_title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
